ipva.title: IPVA 2026 (Vehicle Tax)

reason.bev: SP: passenger BEVs are not exempt solely because they are electric. General 4% scenario.
reason.fuel: SP: gasoline-only or diesel hybrids do not qualify for the ethanol/flex benefit.
reason.technical: Benefit pending: requires ethanol/flex, total electric power ≥40 kW, voltage ≥150 V and energy recovery. Combined horsepower is not proof.
reason.technicalFail: Available technical data do not meet all SP hybrid benefit requirements.
reason.threshold: The estimated base exceeds this year's benefit ceiling. Catalog price does not determine used-vehicle eligibility.
reason.eligible: Available technical data meet the requirements and the estimated base is within the ceiling. Confirm fiscal value, version and recognition by Sefaz; exemption is not guaranteed.
reason.futureCeiling: Future annual ceiling not yet recorded: tax not calculated. Neither the benefit nor full taxation is assumed.
reason.classification: Fiscal class pending: the catalog's commercial category does not distinguish trucks, buses, single-cab pickups and other vehicles.
reason.unreviewed: This state's rules are still under review. No legacy rate or exemption is assumed.
reason.period: Tax year outside the validated calculation period.
reason.invalidBase: Missing or invalid taxable base; a zero value does not mean exemption.
reason.general: Rate based on the available fiscal class, assuming private use and no individual benefits.

ipva.baseDisclaimer: Annual estimate on catalog price (or TCO depreciation), not the official taxable value/invoice. Private use; general class assumed for non-commercial catalog vehicles without proven classification. No acquisition-month proration.
ipva.otherBenefits: Disability, taxi, school transport, rental company, vehicle age, immunities and municipal refunds require additional data and are not included. A state does not identify the municipality or owner circumstances.
ipva.paymentDisclaimer: Payment discounts not included. SP provided 3% for used vehicles paid in full by the January 2026 deadline: not a permanent or post-deadline discount. Check the official calendar and assessment.
ipva.schedule: Statutory schedule for eligible hybrids: 0% in 2025/2026, 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028, 3% in 2029 and 4% from 2030. 2026 reference ceiling: R$ 261,154.45; future IPCA-adjusted ceilings are not assumed.
ipva.reviewed: SP rules reviewed on {{date}}. Other states await audit.
ipva.tcoPartial: Partial TCO — IPVA is unavailable for years marked — and excluded from both vehicles in those years. Totals, cost/km, savings and net result include only calculable tax years; this is not a complete tax comparison.
ipva.tcoScenario: Eligibility or ceiling pending for uncalculated years. Neither 4% nor unproven discounts are assumed in those years; the 2026 estimate does not confirm future benefits.
ipva.tcoBasis: Annual IPVA estimated on depreciated values for each calendar tax year. No personal benefits, refunds or payment discounts; confirm fiscal bases and classification for both vehicles with Sefaz.
ipva.projectionHelp: Only for models with estimated SP/2026 eligibility: applies the statutory schedule to future years, assuming the model still meets each year's requirements and ceiling. Uncheck to exclude years without a calculable tax estimate in the available data.
ipva.projectionDisclaimer: * Future rates and amounts are projected assuming continued benefit eligibility. Future ceilings are not confirmed in the data: the 2026 ceiling is not frozen and Sefaz eligibility is not guaranteed.
ipva.projectionTotals: Totals, savings, cost/km and net result marked * include projected amounts. These are conditional results, not determined tax assessments. Years without technical evidence remain uncalculated.
ipva.projectionTable: IPVA by tax year · * conditional projection; totals include projected amounts
ipva.annualRates: IPVA by tax year — amounts in R$ and rates
ipva.projectedRate: Projected rate, conditional on eligibility and the future ceiling

methodology.title: Calculation Methodology
methodology.subtitle: Data sources, assumptions and formulas behind the catalog, savings simulator, TCO and route planner.
methodology.sourcesCarregados: Carregados — optional official external map, loaded only by an explicit visitor action under the platform's policies. Cited market indicators were consulted on {{date}}, with no automatic refresh, addition to the local dataset or integration into our planner. Totals across pages may differ in scope or date. The public API does not provide coordinates; no Carregados station dataset was imported.
methodology.sourcesChargers: EV map and routes — the partial local dataset combines the April 2026 OCM archive, public OCM listings consulted in November and the November 8, 2026 OSM/Geofabrik extract, retaining their own licenses and credits. This is not a complete national OCM synchronization. The map includes AC, DC and missing electrical details without assuming power or connectors. Counts refer to location records, not sockets or field-verified unique addresses; different sources may list the same place. A recent import does not make old data current: archive, consultation, extract and source-reported update dates are distinct. OSM nodes retain their published positions; area centers are explicitly approximate. OSM/Overpass supplements area search; failures or empty results do not erase loaded points. The planner retains stricter DC power, connector, access and reported-age criteria. Unsourced legacy records remain excluded from routes. Sources, licenses and dates do not confirm physical position, access or live availability. Approximate positions use text search. Check with the operator before travelling.
methodology.sourcesIntro: All calculations start from public and official sources, with the reference date displayed on the site itself.
methodology.sourcesPbev: PBEV/INMETRO — range, energy consumption (MJ/km) and power per model. Reference {{ref}}.
methodology.hybridIntro: Hybrids use the car's own official consumption (Inmetro/PBEV): energy in MJ/km converted to kWh/100km and sustain-mode km/L (city). Category averages apply only as fallback and for the comparison combustion car.
methodology.hybridCombined: Combined PHEV: electric share α = PBEV electric range ÷ the car's combined range. Cost = α×km at official kWh/100km + (1−α)×km at official km/L.
methodology.hybridUtilization: No charging-habit input: combined range is manufacturer-declared (e.g. NEDC) or derived from official tank + Inmetro km/L; without it, full utilization (electric × 30 days) applies.
methodology.hybridHev: HEV: fuel only (no electric leg). Cost = km/month ÷ official km/L × price per liter.
methodology.hybridMaint: TCO: PHEV uses combustion service cost every {{km}}; HEV follows the combustion schedule (10,000 km).
methodology.sourcesPrices: Prices — Guia PBEV market research, history through {{through}}. {{disclaimer}}
methodology.sourcesAneel: Electricity — ANEEL homologated tariffs (B1 residential, TE + TUSD, no ICMS and no tariff flag), main utility per state. Reference {{date}}.
methodology.sourcesAnp: Fuel — average resale prices (SHPC) per state, ANP. Reference {{date}}.
methodology.sourcesIpva: IPVA — SP rules reviewed on {{date}}, using legislation and Sefaz requirements. Other states under review: calculations unavailable, with no presumed exemptions.
methodology.energyIntro: The electric cost uses a weighted average rate between residential AC charging and public DC charging:
methodology.energyFormula: average rate = AC price × (1 − DC%) + DC price × DC%
methodology.energyNote: The DC% slider defines the fraction of charging done at public stations. The default per-category consumption (kWh/100 km) can be replaced with your measured real-world consumption.
methodology.fuelIntro: The combustion comparison uses the reference consumption per category (km/L, PBEV/INMETRO cycle of equivalent vehicles):
methodology.fuelEthanol: Ethanol: volumetric consumption is {{factor}}× higher than gasoline's, reducing the effective km/L.
methodology.fuelEthanolOfficial: Flex: each car's official ethanol figure applies (city, Inmetro); the ÷1.30 estimate only covers the generic comparison car.
methodology.fuelFormula: cost = (km ÷ km/L) × price per liter · electric cost = (km ÷ 100) × kWh/100 km × average rate
methodology.ipvaIntro: Model and state trigger assessment of powertrain, fuel and technical evidence. SP: trucks 1.5%; buses/minibuses and single-cab pickups 2%; other vehicles 4%, before benefits. The catalog commercial category is not a fiscal classification.
methodology.ipvaFormula: Estimated IPVA = estimated base × tax-year rate, subject to classification. Missing evidence means neither exemption nor ineligibility: calculation remains pending.
methodology.ipvaExemptionNote: In states with a value cap for exemption, vehicles above the limit pay the standard rate:
methodology.tcoTitle: TCO — total cost of ownership (4 years)
methodology.tcoIntro: The TCO compares the EV with an equivalent combustion vehicle year by year, always on the depreciated vehicle value:
methodology.tcoDeprEv: EV depreciation: {{value}}% per year (38% over 4 years, linear)
methodology.tcoDeprComb: Combustion depreciation: {{value}}% per year (28% over 4 years, linear)
methodology.tcoInsEv: EV insurance: {{value}}% of the depreciated value per year
methodology.tcoInsComb: Combustion insurance: {{value}}% of the depreciated value per year
methodology.tcoMaint: Maintenance: per-service cost by category, proportional to kilometers driven — service every {{evKm}} km for EVs and every {{combKm}} km for combustion.
methodology.tcoIpva: IPVA by calendar tax year on estimated depreciated value, without unproven benefits. If unavailable, excluded from both sides, with totals labeled partial TCO.
methodology.tcoEnergy: Energy/fuel constant over the 4 years, according to the informed monthly mileage.
methodology.tcoResidual: Net advantage subtracts the EV's extra depreciation loss from the operating savings: net advantage = operating savings − (combustion residual value − EV residual value).
methodology.routeIntro: The vehicle's base consumption is derived from PBEV data:
methodology.routeNote: The 0.93 factor represents the usable battery capacity (93% of the gross declared capacity). Per-leg range considers the battery fraction available at departure and arrival, and consumption is adjusted by a conditions multiplier (temperature, terrain and driving style).
methodology.specsIntro: Conventions for the physical specifications shown on the spec sheet and comparison:
methodology.specsDimensions: Dimensions (length, width, height and wheelbase) in millimeters, per the manufacturer's official website or press release; width without side mirrors.
methodology.specsWeight: Curb weight (vehicle ready to drive, with fluids and full tank/charger), in kilograms.
methodology.specsTrunk: Trunk capacity in liters as declared by the manufacturer; measurement methods may vary.
methodology.specsClearance: Unladen ground clearance, in millimeters — the measurement with underbody accessories is typically lower.
methodology.limitsPbev: PBEV range is measured on a standardized cycle; real consumption varies with weather, speed, load and HVAC use.
methodology.limitsPrices: Prices and rates are indicative and vary by region, utility and dealership.
methodology.limitsTaxes: IPVA rates and exemptions change every year; confirm with your state's Sefaz.
methodology.limitsNotAdvice: Estimates do not constitute purchase or investment advice.
